I care about the parts that keep systems trustworthy in production: validation, monitoring, recovery and compliance.

research.title: Explainable AI-Driven Tomato Disease Diagnosis with Agentic Reasoning
research.venue: MSc in Computing (Artificial Intelligence) · Dublin City University
research.summary: A farmer-facing diagnosis system that combines explainable AI, a 5-stage LLaMA3 reasoning pipeline and English→Irish translation, so growers can see why the model reached a diagnosis and what to do next.
research.abstract: Plant disease diagnosis remains critical for agricultural productivity, yet deep learning models' black-box nature limits farmer trust. This paper presents an integrated system combining explainable AI (XAI), structured reasoning, and neural machine translation for farmer-facing tomato disease diagnosis. We train a ResNet18 model with frozen backbone on 18,160 leaf images achieving 92.3% accuracy — our efficient training approach (20 min CPU-only, no GPU) enables rapid replication by researchers and adaptation to new crops without expensive infrastructure. Three XAI methods are evaluated, with Grad-CAM achieving 91.3% center focus score. Our contribution is a farmer-friendly interpretation layer transforming technical heatmaps into actionable visual reports with zoom panels and urgency-coded recommendations. A 5-step structured reasoning pipeline using LLaMA3 generates contextualized advice with automatic fallback to rule-based templates. For Irish agricultural contexts, we implement Helsinki-NLP neural translation (English→Irish) with BLEU 52.3 and chrF 61.8, validated against 1,800+ curated terms. A Gradio web application provides bilingual diagnosis with real-time translation quality transparency, bridging AI capability and farmer usability.
